shared_elements: upright monolithic form with an implied anthropomorphic body (head/shoulders/torso)
shallow low-relief carving covering the front/back surface
creature heads shown in profile (bird-like/beaked forms)
horizontal band of repeated geometric elements crossing the surface
curved paired arcs/loops in the upper zone
elongated curving forms resembling a limb or snake
justification: Both surfaces present a large upright stone of implied anthropomorphic shape whose broad surface is covered with shallow, schematic low relief organised into stacked zones: a row of paired arcs/curved motifs near the top, a horizontal band of repeated geometric marks, and beneath it profile creature-heads and prominent ring or disc motifs. The differences are in the specific creatures and relations: B shows clearly readable animals (quadrupeds in profile, a beaked bird, an elongated snake-like form arranged in a vertical sequence and touching the pillar's edges), whereas A's motifs are far more abstract and symmetrical curvilinear glyphs with no comparable animal-to-animal interactions.
